recommendation.name: Finite Discrete Causal DAG and Identifiable Back-Door Adjustment Scope
core: Finite small categorical DAG,explicit treatment/outcome and supplied adjustment set
No descendant of treatment in adjustment; d-separation after removing outgoing treatment edges
Exact rational joint normalization,standardization and observational comparison
Explicit overlap/positivity failures and no causal estimate for unsupported adjustment
All-observed complete-joint factorization compatibility check; causal truth still an assumption
Latent graphs diagnostic/unsupported in first core; no general nonidentifiability theorem
recommendation.scientific_limit: A graph is an input causal assumption,not a conclusion from correlations. Graphical identification,statistical estimability and empirical causal validity are separate.

supported_candidate: Original synthetic finite exact tables and assumed causal DAGs
Supplied-set back-door diagnostics and exact standardization
experimental: Interpreting synthetic effects as domain predictions

conventions: Back-door surgery removes OUTGOING treatment arrows; do-intervention structural oracle removes incoming assignment mechanism. Do not confuse the two.
A failed supplied-set criterion means unsupported by this method,not a proof of universal nonidentifiability. Never compute adjustment just because a Z column exists.
Positive P(Z=z) requires positive P(X=x,Z=z) for every requested treatment level; zero-mass strata omitted transparently,not fabricated. No smoothing or extrapolation.

Finite normalized joint must account for zero cells and all declared states. In an all-observed DAG, verify exact factorization compatibility over full joint before certifying the table/model pair. Compatibility does not establish causal truth.
Explicit graph/consistency/exchangeability assumptions; no interference or ill-defined treatment interpretation is established by file validation.
No real human dataset ingestion; self-authored synthetic tables and hash/rights declarations only.
source_disagreements: DoWhy offers more identification/adjustment strategies than the original sufficient back-door criterion. First core deliberately checks one supplied set and may conservatively decline otherwise identifiable effects.
Potential-outcome and graphical formulations express related assumptions differently; keep consistency,exchangeability and positivity explicit.
Latest What If author link is2026; indexed2025/2024 passages do not certify access to latest complete text.

literal_anchors.independent_oracle: Enumerate Z in{0,1}, E_X in0..3,E_Y in0..9,all80 equally likely. X=1 iff E_X<(1 if Z=0 else3);Y=1 iff E_Y<1+2X+4Z. Force X=0/1 before computing Y for interventional oracle; does not call adjustment implementation.
